# Harness Execution Summary

The harness achieves moderate accuracies across three datasets (39-56% train, 52-54% eval) using few-shot in-context learning with demonstration selection. A consistent failure pattern shows the model reliably identifies "closest demonstrations" according to its selection logic, yet these selections fail to guide correct predictions—the demonstrated examples don't encode the actual task structure. As learning progresses, context size grows substantially (from ~200 chars to ~4600 chars) without corresponding accuracy gains, suggesting that simply accumulating examples doesn't improve reasoning. The reasoning traces reveal superficial matching: the model selects plausible-sounding demonstrations but lacks a principled strategy to extract or apply classification rules from them. Recommend investigating the demonstration selection mechanism itself—whether it prioritizes semantic relevance, label patterns, or only surface-level word overlap—and consider alternate approaches such as in-context prompt refinement or explicit task-structure learning over raw similarity-based selection.
